idiom_name: phantom type-parameter flags per required property + free-function terminal guard
implementation_notes: Go 1.18+ generics can express the pattern with marker flags: the builder is typed builder[Name Flag, URL Flag] over a sealed Flag interface with Set and Unset marker structs, each WithX method re-instantiates only its own slot, and the flags are never stored, so transitions are plain conversions. The decisive difference from Rust is that Go methods cannot be declared for one instantiation only: the terminal guard has to be a free function pinned to builder[Set, Set] (or an interface trick), because the method set is identical for every instantiation. Values are copyable, so a stale builder remains usable - treat the guarantee as 'the final call cannot be written too early', not as consumption.
pitfalls: Methods cannot be specialized per instantiation, so a fluent .Build() is impossible; the all-set requirement must live on a function parameter or an interface method set.
Struct values are copyable: any copy of a Set-flagged builder is still Set, so transitions can be replayed - do not confuse the check with linear ownership.
The flag interface must be sealed with an unexported method, otherwise callers can define their own state types and satisfy the constraint.
